title: The buffer-stock families' shared parameter definitions
description: What the four buffer-stock families' parameter files have in common, as model.md names it. Each family's parameters.schema.json takes these definitions and adds its own family key and constraint. Draft.

period.description: The length of a period, as a label. Every rate and probability in the file is per period.

crra.description: rho, the coefficient of relative risk aversion, greater than 1 as in BST.

types.description: The discount-factor types, in increasing order of beta, with population shares omega summing to one.

survival.description: The survival probability (BST's script L); 1 switches mortality off.

return.description: R, the gross return on assets.

growth.description: The growth factor of permanent income (BST's script G).

prob.description: wp, the probability of the unemployment event each period. With 0, income must be 0 too, so that the file has one written form.

income.description: xi_u, income while unemployed, as a ratio to permanent income; 0 in BST, where it is also the lowest value of the transitory shock xi, though not in general.

employed_shock.description: The law of theta, the employed draw, before the scaling (1 - wp xi_u)/(1 - wp) that keeps the mean of the transitory shock at one.

artificial_constraint.description: The artificial borrowing constraint a_Art, the lowest permitted end-of-period assets as a ratio to permanent income: a number no greater than 0, strictly above the natural constraint a_Nat, which the checker enforces.
